newsitem.title: MOZAMBIQUE: Mideast and African port conditions - Lloyds.
newsitem.headline: Mideast and African port conditions - Lloyds.

text.p: Port conditions from Lloyds Shipping Intelligence Service --

MOZAMBIQUE, April 21 - Nacala - Port working normally. No restrictions on berthing and sailing at night. Draft restrictions 9.5 metres at general cargo berth, 14 metres at container berth. One tug available. Beira - General cargo berths - Working normally. Container/other terminals - Working normally, 24 hour berthing/sailing for vessels up to 140 metres loa, some restrictions for larger vessels and subject to arrangement with port captain. Maximum draft for 24 hour navigation 7.5 metres. Two tugs available. General access channel - Two waverider buoys in approach channel as follows wmon1 19 deg. 66.0460 s 36 deg. 01.6698 e and wmon2 19 deg. 62.6370 s 34 deg. 62.6497 e. Approximate diameter 1 metre. Orange light with a flash frequency, five one-second flashes every 36 seconds.

Maputo - 24 Hour berthing/sailing for vessels up to 120 metres loa, some restrictions for larger vessels and subject to arrangement with port captain. All berths working normally, expected to remain so. Draft restriction in channel 9.0 metres less 0.5 metres plus the rise of tide. Max draft for 24 hour navigation 9 metres.
NAMIBIA, April 21 - Walvis Bay - Working normally.
NIGERIA, April 22 - Bonny - Due to industrial action by a sub-contractor, terminal has declared force majeure on several cargoes.

SOUTH AFRICA, April 21 - Richard's Bay - General cargo berths - Working normally. Bulk import berths - 702 Extremely congested. Berth 701 has openings on Alusaf berth but vessels from 702 are being slotted into 701 to release pressure. Bulk export berths - Working normally, no major delays. Bulk coal - 4 Vessels berthed, 1 arriving 21/4. A further 21 vessels due up to and including 28/4, with berthing delays of approx 24-36 hours at present. Durban - Container terminal some vessels experiencing delays of up to 48 hours, others berthing on arrival.

Point/New pier/Maydon wharf berths - Working normally for general cargo vessels. Maize terminal (Maydon wharf 8) - No vessels. Bunker supplies - Product available but this could change daily due to bunching of vessels. Dry-dock/floating dock - 70 percent committed for April and 70 percent for May. East London - General cargo/combi terminal berths - Busy but no delays expected at this stage. Dry-dock open for booking tankers, 1 expected weekly. Wheat imports - 1 Vessel due 28/4.

Port Elizabeth - Working normally, 5 vessels in port. No delays expected on general, tanker, ore or fruit berths. Container berth - Two berths available with 2 gantry cranes. Berth fully occupied until 23/4, but no delays expected. Cape Town - Breakbulk (general cargo) - Working normally, vessels operating on arrival. Fruit berths - Fully occupied. Container terminal - Some delays due to computer lines being down and Portnet planners refusing to plan vessels manually. Bunker berths - Due to non-availability of fuel oil in Durban and heavy fog in Cape Town, substantial delays in berthing/bunkering. Dry-docks and repair quays fully occupied. Booking essential. Saldanha Bay - Working normally.

TUNISIA, April 19 - Sousse - One vessel in port discharging large bags, no waiting time, no vessels waiting. Gabes - No labour problems. One bulk fertiliser vessel loading at berth. Sfax - Six vessels in port operating of which 4 discharging (1 bulk sulphur, 1 bulk bitumen, 1 timber, 1 general cargo). 2 Loading (1 bulk olive oil, 1 bulk olive cake). Tunis - Five vessels in port of which 3 awaiting instructions, 1 discharging general cargo, 1 discharging wood. Rades - Three ro-ro vessels in port. La Goulette - North side - 1 Vessel discharging pvc, 1 maize, 1 general cargo vessel, 1 passenger vessel. South side - 1 Vessel discharging grain, 1 loading clinker, 2 vessels in roads.

April 22 - Bizerte - No berthing delays/congestion/strikes. Five vessels operating of which 3 discharging (1 sugar, 1 crude oil, 1 wheat), 2 loading steel. Zarzis - No berthing delays/congestion/strikes. No vessels.

UNITED ARAB EMIRATES, April 13-19 - Dubai - No labour problems. 182 Vessels of which 82 containers, 12 general cargo, 1 general cargo/containers, 3 bulk carriers, 7 car carriers, 15 tankers, 3 naval vessels, 2 U.A.E. naval vessels, 4 bunkering/under repair/taking on stores etc., 17 barges, 9 tugs, 17 supply boats, 2 passenger vessels, 1 lpg tanker, 1 chemical tanker, 1 survey vessel, 1 ferry, 1 refrigerator vessel, 3 fishing trawlers. 4 Vessels discharging at berth (3 general cargo, 1 tanker). 9 Vessels under repair/laid-up (1 containers, 1 general cargo, 7 tankers).

YEMEN, April 22 - Hodeidah - Berths 2, 4, 5, 6 and 7 are occupied, the other berths are vacant. 5 Vessels berthed of which 2 flour, 1 containers, 1 bulk wheat, 1 steel, 1 flour vessel anchored. Berthing delays, general cargo/containers up to 1 day, bagged cargo up to 2 days, bulk cargo up to 6 days. Mokha - No vessels berthed, none anchored, no delays.
